assign.request: Two core bugs found by today's builds. BUG 1: width:"full" collapses the SITE SIDEBAR to 0px (full = flex: 1 0 100% on .page-column-body; pressure escapes .pages into the .app flex row). BUG 2: View.href(undefined) falls into attr()'s GETTER branch and returns null; href(undefined|null) should be a chainable no-op. Fence: core/Page/Page.css, core/View/View.js, doc lines. Verify headless at 1280/1920/3440 with before/after sidebar numbers.
steps: reproduce both bugs headless, capture before numbers
diagnose bug 1 at the cause (the flex chain from .page-column-body to .app)
fix bug 1 with the narrowest rule in Page.css
diagnose bug 2 (href/attr arity) and state the blast radius
fix bug 2 at the honest level
verify headless: sidebar numbers 1280/1920/3440 + full still owns its row
regression sweep: /framework/, a Doc page, /imagine/, uses/split, zero console errors
docs: columns.md, View doc, decisions.md; land

log.msg: BUG 1 IS NOT A BUG. Every .sidebar enumerated on four routes at 1280: index 0 is the SITE ROOT homepage topic sidebar, 0x0 because its own page is display:none by the arrangement contract on every route that is not /. The real framework sidebar (index 1) is 229x900 on ALL of them - /framework/ homepage, finder root, the full column, a Doc page. querySelector(.sidebar) finds the hidden one first; that is the 0x0 that was reported.

full still owns its row, unchanged: 1051 / 1677 / 3166 at 1280 / 1920 / 3440 (3166 matches doc/columns.md 2026-08-27). Sidebar 229 / 243 / 274 at the same widths, cold load AND click-through, identical to the finder root with no full column open. Also stamped page-column-full on a HOST body (the untested combination imagine/vary/scroll/full names) - sidebar held at all three widths.

assign.now: bug 1 closed as not-a-bug; diagnosing View.href arity

log.msg: BUG 2 fixed at attr(), the honest level: the getter/setter branch now reads arguments.length, not is.def(value). One argument reads; two write, and a nullish value writes nothing and returns this. href takes ...url so the arity is forwarded and href() is still the getter. Blast radius audited first: every .attr( in public/ - two getter-form callers (both single-argument, untouched), zero passing a literal null/undefined, and zero anywhere using the return value as anything but this.

Proved both ways headless. Old methods put back on View.prototype in the live page: demo.tree().preview() on a url-less nav THREW Cannot read properties of null (reading attr). With the fix: renders, no href attribute, aria-label written. href(x) sets, href() reads back, href(null) is a chainable no-op, attr(k) getter and the idempotent re-set all unchanged.

Regression sweep clean: 7 routes x 1280/1920/3440 plus 11 more at 1280 - zero console errors and zero unexpected 4xx. Sidebar 229/243/274 and full 1051/1677/3166 on every full route; /framework/, a Doc page, /imagine/, uses/split all unchanged. The only 404s seen are Page.load() page.js probes (by design) and /imagine/screens/ files another session is mid-build on.

assign.outcome:
**One real bug, one false alarm.** `View.attr()` branched on the VALUE, not the arity; `width: "full"` never touched the sidebar.

**Bug 2 - fixed at the cause.** `attr()` asked `is.def(value)`, which is the same question as "was a value passed" only until the value you pass IS `undefined` - an optional url. It called that a question, returned the attribute (`null` on a fresh element), and `.href(nav.url).attr(...)` died two calls later ([ext/demo `exhibit.js:143`](/framework/ext/demo/)). One argument reads now; two write, and a nullish value writes nothing and returns `this`. `href(...url)` forwards the arity so `href()` is still the getter.

[attr](/framework/core/View/api/attr/) - the fix live, with the audit - [href](/framework/core/View/api/href/) - [View decisions](/framework/core/View/doc/decisions.md)

**Blast radius, audited before choosing the level:** every `.attr(` in `public/` - **two** getter-form callers (both single-argument, both untouched), **zero** passing a literal `null`/`undefined`, **zero** anywhere using the return value as anything but `this`.

**Bug 1 - not a bug, and Page.css is untouched.** The site ROOT is a topic with a sidebar of its own, so `querySelector(".sidebar")` finds THAT one first and it is 0x0 on every route except `/` - its page is hidden by the arrangement contract. The real sidebar holds on every route, `full` or not:

| | 1280 | 1920 | 3440 |
|---|---|---|---|
| sidebar, `full` column open | **229** | **243** | **274** |
| sidebar, nothing open / `/framework/` / a Doc page | 229 | 243 | 274 |
| the `full` column's own row | 1051 | 1677 | 3166 |

3166 at 3440 is `doc/columns.md`'s own 2026-08-27 number. Cold load and click-through both, and stamping `page-column-full` on a HOST's body - the one combination no page ships - changed neither number. The trap is written down: [columns.md](/framework/core/Page/doc/columns/).

![the sidebar holding beside a full column at 1280](sidebar-holds-1280.png)

[1920](sidebar-holds-1920.png) - [3440](sidebar-holds-3440.png) - [the full column, live](/framework/core/Page/overview/columns/finder/guides/words/full/)

**Verified:** 7 routes x 1280/1920/3440 plus 11 more at 1280 - zero console errors, zero unexpected 4xx. The old methods put back on `View.prototype` in the live page reproduce the throw; with the fix the same call renders.

**Left:** `core/View/readme.md` gets no line (outside the fence) - the `attr` trap is only in `doc/`. No `removeAttr`: `attr(name, null)` now writes nothing at all rather than sometimes writing the string `"null"`, and nothing in `public/` wants a remove.
